hypothesis: Giving canonical SOL Range Onset higher static fallback priority than HT-Breakout may improve the shared SOL lifecycle path without adding a gate or evicting an open position.
decision: Reject the static-priority-only update. The current and Range-Onset-first arms accepted identical lifecycle IDs and produced identical economics in development and the already-opened descriptive final block because HT-Breakout and Range Onset had zero shared entry timestamps. Keep v25 priorities and protected live positions unchanged. The next bounded SOL experiment is an exact historical-to-live HT-Breakout decision-parity audit followed, only if parity holds, by one minimal causal entry-timing challenger under unchanged exits and costs. Preserve canonical Range Onset without relaxation as a separately attributed sparse route. Do not increase leverage, notional, or hold duration to offset the reconstructed dense route's negative economics.
falsifier: The no-priority-effect conclusion is invalidated by omitted or changed source lifecycles, evidence hash mismatch, a nonzero accepted-trade symmetric difference, or a runtime contract that permits priority-based eviction or slot reservation. The HT-Breakout component diagnosis must be revised if exact historical/live decision parity fails or if sufficiently sized after-cost forward evidence becomes positive on both sides without largest-winner dependence. Execution authority or any runtime mutation invalidates this record.
limitations: The opened final block was previously inspected and is descriptive rather than a sealed holdout.
